final_candidates.decision_summary: G121 lies in the conserved glycine-rich GDPIGDQ loop near the FAD/catalytic core; a bulky charged Arg should sterically and electrostatically disrupt cofactor binding, strongly favoring loss-of-function.
D223 sits in the conserved FFEADT motif where acidic residues commonly serve as catalytic acid/base or cofactor contacts; D->A is a clean catalytic knockout with retained fold.
R157 is a conserved arginine likely coordinating substrate/cofactor; removing the charged sidechain should impair catalysis while preserving overall fold.

stop_reason.detail: No evidence tools available and top motif-based catalytic candidates are stable, so additional rounds add little value.

history.rationale: Arg157 in the RGDP/active-site region likely coordinates substrate phosphate or FAD; charge removal to Ala is expected to strongly impair catalysis.
R157 is a conserved arginine likely involved in substrate/cofactor coordination; Ala removes the charged sidechain, plausibly impairing catalysis while preserving fold.
The FFPPR motif near residue 66 is highly conserved in MTHFR; the proline is structurally rigid and its substitution can distort the catalytic fold.
P66 may enforce a turn, but P->A is often tolerated and less reliably abolishes activity, so it is deprioritized.
The glycine in the GDP catalytic loop needs backbone flexibility; introducing a bulky charged Arg should sterically break the active-site geometry.
G121 lies in the conserved GDP(G121DPIGDQ) glycine-rich loop near the FAD/catalytic core; a bulky charged Arg should sterically and electrostatically disrupt cofactor binding and abolish activity.
Phe65 in the conserved FFPPR motif is buried and hydrophobic; a charged Asp substitution should destabilize the catalytic core and disrupt function.
F65 in the EFFPPRT region is likely buried/structural; introducing a charged Asp could destabilize but effect on activity is less certain than active-site substitutions.
Asp223 in the ITQLFF region may participate in substrate binding within the TIM-barrel; alanine substitution could reduce catalytic competence.
D223 sits in the FFEADT catalytic motif; conserved acidic residues here are common general acid/base or metal/cofactor contacts, and D->A is a clean catalytic knockout mutation.
The CCRQR cysteine cluster around 129-130 may have structural/redox roles near the active site; a bulky Tyr can misfold this region and impair activity.
C130 in the CCRQR motif could be functional but its exact role is uncertain and Tyr substitution effect is ambiguous, so it stays low.
The MALRGDP region around residues 145-150 is a conserved active-site-adjacent loop; targeting a polar residue here provides an alternative catalytic-disruption candidate to diversify the pool.
